prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural‑language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), visible actions and interactions, and the setting; keep the caption concrete and image‑centered and avoid speculation or subjective judgments. State whether each person or object is stationary or moving; when describing motion give horizontal direction first then vertical (for example, "walking from left to right," "moving toward the camera while descending"), specify the visible phase of motion when apparent (starting/ascending/peaking/descending/landing) and whether motions are simultaneous or sequential, and describe each moving subject’s trajectory relative to the main subject (passing to his right, approaching from behind, moving alongside) and relative to the camera. For interactions with objects or structures state exactly how the subject is using them (holding/gripping/resting on/pulling/supporting/bracing/leaning on), include which hand (left/right) and side, and indicate whether the hand is in contact, gripping, or merely near or in motion versus resting. Describe body posture using concrete camera‑relative terms (standing, weight shifted onto left/right leg, slightly leaning forward/back when clearly visible, seated, reclining, crouching, mid‑jump, arms outstretched, knees bent) and specify orientation to the camera (facing the camera, in profile, back to the camera); prefer neutral, observable stance descriptors rather than implied effort. Report facial expressions or visible affect only when clearly evident using observable detail (open‑mouthed, smiling with teeth visible, furrowed brow) and identify gaze targets (eyes looking down at the object in his hands, gaze directed at the camera). Clarify precise spatial relationships, counts and arrangement of people or vehicles (two people side by side, a row of three boats), proximity and scale (a few feet/meters apart, clustered closely, towering behind), and use "in front of," "over," or "directly above/overhead" instead of ambiguous "above." Describe lighting, shadows, and visible surface textures with observable cues and approximate shadow direction or length (bright direct sunlight casting long shadows toward the lower left, diffuse overcast, wet pavement, reflections, motion blur). Output exactly one single sentence.
